beats.label: S1 · The hidden algorithm
beats.text: Richard, a low-level Hooli coder, ships a music app that hides a world-class compression algorithm; Belson notices and secretly begins cloning it as Nucleus.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the algorithm as the show's central object of desire and establishes Hooli as its permanent opponent.

beats.label: S1 · The founder's choice
beats.text: Faced with a $10M Hooli buyout or a $200K seed from billionaire Peter Gregory, Richard turns down the check and takes the investment to run the company himself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Defines Richard's founder identity and locks Peter Gregory in as the show's original patron.

beats.label: S1 · Jared and Big Head switch sides
beats.text: Ex-Hooli assistant Jared joins to run operations; Belson counters by promoting Richard's mediocre friend Big Head to publicly claim him as Pied Piper's co-founder.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Jared as the ops brain and sets up Big Head's role as Belson's ongoing lawsuit chess piece.

beats.label: S1 · Erlich on the board
beats.text: A drunken toga party ends with Erlich Bachman permanently on the board, giving Richard's opinionated landlord structural power over the company.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Erlich's board seat is the reason he keeps overriding Richard for the rest of the series.

beats.label: S1 · Nucleus at Battlefield
beats.text: At TechCrunch Battlefield, Hooli reveals Nucleus with the same compression score and more features; Pied Piper looks beaten before Richard even walks on.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Frames Hooli as the near-equal competitor and sets the stakes for Richard's algorithmic breakthrough.

beats.label: S1 · The breakthrough
beats.text: A crass whiteboard joke sparks a real math breakthrough; Richard rewrites the algorithm overnight to a Weissman score of 5.2 and Pied Piper wins Battlefield.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The 5.2 score is the technical foundation the rest of the series inherits.

beats.label: S1 · The hard part starts
beats.text: Belson is publicly humiliated. Monica warns Richard the hard part starts now, and he vomits into an alley behind the venue.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Signals the tonal shift from underdog story into the real fight for the company that defines S2.

cliffhanger.text: Pied Piper has won Battlefield and Richard is now running a real company he has no idea how to run, with a publicly humiliated Hooli plotting its next move.
questions: How does Belson retaliate for losing to Richard in front of the whole industry?
Can Richard actually lead a funded company, or does the panic get the better of him?
What happens now that serious investors and expectations are circling Pied Piper?

characters.name: Richard Hendricks
characters.line: Nervous coder whose compression algorithm just won Battlefield; now the reluctant CEO of a funded company.

characters.name: Erlich Bachman
characters.line: Loud incubator owner with a permanent Pied Piper board seat and a 10% stake.

characters.name: Jared Dunn
characters.line: Fastidious Hooli defector running Pied Piper's business and operations.

characters.name: Bertram Gilfoyle
characters.line: Bearded satanist systems engineer at Pied Piper.

characters.name: Dinesh Chugtai
characters.line: Pied Piper coder locked in constant rivalry with Gilfoyle.

characters.name: Nelson "Big Head" Bighetti
characters.line: Richard's mediocre friend, promoted at Hooli as a fake Pied Piper co-founder to strengthen Belson's claim.

characters.name: Gavin Belson
characters.line: Hooli CEO publicly humiliated by Pied Piper and now Richard's real enemy.

characters.name: Peter Gregory
characters.line: Eccentric billionaire VC whose $200K seed made Pied Piper possible.

characters.name: Monica Hall
characters.line: Peter Gregory's associate at Raviga and Richard's outside ally.

beats.label: S2 · Peter dies, Hooli sues
beats.text: Peter Gregory dies suddenly; Raviga installs the equally odd Laurie Bream, and at Peter's funeral Hooli files an IP lawsuit against Pied Piper.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Loses the show's founding patron and launches the lawsuit that defines the whole season.

beats.label: S2 · The Hanneman bailout
beats.text: The lawsuit spooks every VC. Richard takes a $5M rescue from flashy billionaire Russ Hanneman, at the cost of two seats on the board.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Hanneman as an unstable partner whose money and board seats will keep steering the company.

beats.label: S2 · Nucleus flops, End Frame steals
beats.text: Belson launches Nucleus on a UFC broadcast and it fails on live TV; meanwhile a rival called End Frame tricks the team into revealing the algorithm.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Nucleus's public failure weakens Belson, and End Frame becomes the season's new outside threat.

beats.label: S2 · Big Head at Hooli XYZ
beats.text: To bolster the lawsuit, Belson promotes clueless Big Head to co-head Hooli XYZ; when Bannercheck resigns in protest, Big Head becomes sole head of a shell project.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Big Head's absurd promotion track sets up the severance money that reshapes the ownership fight later.

beats.label: S2 · Arbitration reverses
beats.text: In binding arbitration, Richard admits testing his algorithm on a Hooli laptop; the judge rules for Hooli, then reverses when Hooli's employment contracts are ruled illegal.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The reversal saves the algorithm and simultaneously guts Hooli, resetting the balance of power.

beats.label: S2 · Raviga fires Richard
beats.text: Raviga buys out Hanneman's stake, giving Laurie three of five board seats; she uses the majority to fire Richard as CEO of his own company.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Richard from the CEO chair and hands the company to Raviga, the setup for all of S3.

beats.label: S2 · Belson before the board
beats.text: The same ruling voids over half of Hooli's employment contracts; Belson is summoned before his own board to answer for the disaster he built.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Belson's grip on Hooli in doubt just as Richard loses his grip on Pied Piper.

cliffhanger.text: Pied Piper survived the lawsuit but Raviga has taken control and fired Richard as CEO; Belson has been called before Hooli's board to answer for the Nucleus disaster.
questions: Who runs Pied Piper now, and what do they turn it into?
Can Richard take his own company back from the board that just fired him?
Does Belson survive his own board meeting, and if not, who takes Hooli?

characters.name: Richard Hendricks
characters.line: Founder just fired as CEO by Raviga; still on the team he built.

characters.name: Erlich Bachman
characters.line: Still on Pied Piper's board and still hosting the company from his house.

characters.name: Jared Dunn
characters.line: Operations lead, now living in a neighbour's guest house next door to the incubator.

characters.name: Bertram Gilfoyle
characters.line: Built and runs Pied Piper's homemade server infrastructure.

characters.name: Dinesh Chugtai
characters.line: Pied Piper coder, thoroughly humiliated all season and going nowhere.

characters.name: Nelson "Big Head" Bighetti
characters.line: Sole head of Hooli's shell XYZ lab, promoted through failure and mentored by a corporate guru.

characters.name: Gavin Belson
characters.line: Hooli CEO facing his own board after Nucleus flopped and his lawsuit collapsed.

characters.name: Laurie Bream
characters.line: Raviga's managing partner and Pied Piper's new controlling shareholder.

characters.name: Monica Hall
characters.line: Raviga associate and Richard's inside line at the firm that just fired him.

characters.name: Russ Hanneman
characters.line: Brash billionaire who bought in cheap and just cashed out to Raviga.

beats.label: S3 · Jack Barker and the box
beats.text: Raviga's new CEO Jack Barker forces Pied Piper to sell a hardware box instead of a platform; Richard runs his platform vision as a secret skunkworks project.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Frames the entire season as Richard's vision versus Jack's revenue plan.

beats.label: S3 · Belson overpays for End Frame
beats.text: Belson overpays $250M for End Frame's middle-out compression, repricing Pied Piper's platform above the box deal; Laurie fires Jack and reinstates Richard as CEO.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Belson accidentally hands Richard the argument that puts him back in the CEO seat.

beats.label: S3 · Bachmanity's million-dollar luau
beats.text: Erlich and Big Head form 'Bachmanity' and blow a million on a luau at Alcatraz; a rogue manager has quietly embezzled Big Head into bankruptcy.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The debt is what forces Erlich to sell his stock, which is what unlocks the finale ownership swap.

beats.label: S3 · Launch without users
beats.text: The platform launches to half a million downloads but almost no daily users; Jared secretly hires a Bangladeshi click farm to fake the numbers.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The invisible DAU problem is the ticking bomb under the whole back half of the season.

beats.label: S3 · The click farm confession
beats.text: Richard reveals the click-farm fraud to a Coleman Blair investment round; the deal collapses and Pied Piper's credibility with VCs collapses with it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kills the compression platform's future funding path and forces the coming pivot.

beats.label: S3 · Erlich and Big Head buy the company
beats.text: Raviga puts its stake up for sale and Belson bids to bury Pied Piper; flush from selling Code/Rag, Erlich and Big Head outbid him by a dollar to take control.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Hands Pied Piper's ownership to the two least-qualified people alive, the setup for S4.

beats.label: S3 · Monica in, chat rising
beats.text: Monica, fired for opposing Laurie, joins the team; they realise Dinesh's throwaway video chat app is quietly better than anything Hooli has built.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Points the company at its next pivot and puts Monica inside the tent.

cliffhanger.text: The compression platform is dead and Pied Piper is now owned by Erlich and Big Head after a chain of accidents; Dinesh's throwaway video chat is the company's only real hope.
questions: Does Pied Piper pivot the whole company onto a side-project chat app?
Can Richard lead a company his best friend and his landlord now own?
What does Belson do now that both Nucleus and Endframe have blown up in his face?

characters.name: Richard Hendricks
characters.line: Reinstated CEO whose flagship product just failed; grasping for a next act.

characters.name: Erlich Bachman
characters.line: Improbable co-owner of Pied Piper via a Code/Rag windfall.

characters.name: Nelson "Big Head" Bighetti
characters.line: Improbable co-owner of Pied Piper alongside Erlich.

characters.name: Jared Dunn
characters.line: Operations lead who confessed to secretly running the click farm.

characters.name: Bertram Gilfoyle
characters.line: Systems engineer keeping Pied Piper's infrastructure alive.

characters.name: Dinesh Chugtai
characters.line: Coder whose side-project video chat is suddenly Pied Piper's future.

characters.name: Monica Hall
characters.line: Fired from Raviga for opposing Laurie; now inside Pied Piper.

characters.name: Gavin Belson
characters.line: Hooli CEO badly damaged after burning $250M on Endframe and losing the buyout bid.

characters.name: Laurie Bream
characters.line: Raviga head who removed Richard, then reinstated him, then sold the stake and moved on.

characters.name: Jack Barker
characters.line: Ousted Pied Piper CEO; corporate operator, still around and available.

beats.label: S4 · Richard walks away from CEO
beats.text: Richard steps down as CEO to chase a decentralized 'new internet' alone, giving Dinesh the PiperChat pivot in exchange for the algorithm and the Pied Piper brand.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the new-internet mission that drives every remaining season.

beats.label: S4 · Belson eats the COPPA fine
beats.text: Belson bullies Dinesh into signing PiperChat over to Hooli, then discovers he's inherited a $21B COPPA fine; the board fires him and installs Jack Barker as CEO.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Belson from Hooli and puts Jack Barker back in charge of the rival.

beats.label: S4 · Peter's old patent, Belson's name
beats.text: Richard finds Peter Gregory imagined the same decentralized internet years earlier, and Belson holds the patent; he pitches Belson on building it as revenge on Hooli.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Locks the algorithm and the patent together and lines Belson up as an unlikely partner.

beats.label: S4 · Belson leaves the fight
beats.text: A blood-boy scandal breaks Belson's nerve; he leaves Palo Alto for Tibet and signs the decentralized-internet patent over to Richard, but without any funding.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Frees Richard from Belson and leaves him owning the vision but broke.

beats.label: S4 · Monica's smartphone bet
beats.text: Keenan Feldspar sells his hyped VR startup to Hooli; Monica promises Pied Piper Series A funding if Richard can get the new internet running on real smartphones.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the concrete goal that structures the finale and the funding path that follows.

beats.label: S4 · Hooli-Con and the exploding phones
beats.text: At Hooli-Con, Pied Piper piggybacks on free Wi-Fi to hit its install target; but Hooli's VR keynote explodes phones live, and every affected phone is running Pied Piper.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The install win comes with a hidden liability that drives the finale's cascade.

beats.label: S4 · The refrigerator network
beats.text: Trying to move their server, they find its code has spread across smart fridges into a working distributed network; Bream-Hall funds them and Belson retakes Hooli.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Proves the new internet is real and puts Belson back at Hooli for the next fight.

cliffhanger.text: Pied Piper's decentralized internet unexpectedly works on a network of smart refrigerators; Bream-Hall is funding it, Belson has retaken Hooli, and Erlich is stranded in Tibet.
questions: Can Pied Piper actually turn a fridge accident into real infrastructure?
What does Belson do now that he's back in charge of Hooli?
Does Erlich ever get back from Tibet, and what happens to his stake in the meantime?

characters.name: Richard Hendricks
characters.line: CEO of a company finally aligned with his real vision, freshly funded by Bream-Hall.

characters.name: Jared Dunn
characters.line: Operations lead who moved onto Richard's decentralized project from day one.

characters.name: Bertram Gilfoyle
characters.line: Systems engineer whose refrigerator hack accidentally proved the whole concept.

characters.name: Dinesh Chugtai
characters.line: Coder who briefly ran PiperChat and is now back on the main team.

characters.name: Monica Hall
characters.line: Partner at Bream-Hall, personally sponsoring Pied Piper's Series A.

characters.name: Laurie Bream
characters.line: Founding partner at Bream-Hall alongside Monica.

characters.name: Gavin Belson
characters.line: Back as Hooli CEO after freeing Jack Barker from a Chinese factory hostage crisis.

characters.name: Jack Barker
characters.line: Briefly Hooli CEO after Belson's fall; sidelined again after the China disaster.

characters.name: Nelson "Big Head" Bighetti
characters.line: Now a guest lecturer at Stanford, still peripherally involved with Pied Piper.

characters.name: Erlich Bachman
characters.line: Stranded in a Tibetan opium den, paid up for five years by Belson.

beats.label: S5 · Building the team from scraps
beats.text: Belson corners every distributed-systems engineer in the valley; Richard salvages a team by absorbing two failing startups and coding 48 straight hours to earn their respect.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Pied Piper as a real company with real engineers for the first time.

beats.label: S5 · Jared up, Erlich out
beats.text: Jared is promoted to COO. Jian-Yang forges papers to become Erlich's sole beneficiary and evicts the team from the Hacker Hostel.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the incubator era and installs Jian-Yang as the legal owner of Erlich's assets.

beats.label: S5 · Octopipers and the China clone
beats.text: Pied Piper signs eight 'octopiper' launch partners; but Jian-Yang launches a clone of the new internet from China and one of the octopipers defects to him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Frames Jian-Yang's Chinese operation as the season's real threat, ahead of Belson.

beats.label: S5 · The ICO
beats.text: Bream-Hall's terms leave Pied Piper exposed; on Gilfoyle's idea they launch an ICO, PiedPiperCoin, and Monica quits Bream-Hall to run it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Cuts Pied Piper loose from its VCs and rewires the ownership around the coin.

beats.label: S5 · Yao's majority attack
beats.text: PiperNet starts growing, but the new users are all Yao's Chinese devices, subscribed under Jian-Yang's key, racing to a 51% majority that would seize the network.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Turns the season's slow build into an existential fight over control of the network itself.

beats.label: S5 · Richard gives Belson the company
beats.text: Facing extinction, Richard offers Belson full ownership of Pied Piper in exchange for wiping out Yao's attack; Belson swings it and accepts the company.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Belson in charge of Pied Piper for the first time and sets up the immediate reversal.

beats.label: S5 · Gilfoyle's lockout
beats.text: While Belson gloats, Dinesh and Jared quietly add 80,000 users from another gaming app; Gilfoyle patches Hooli and Yao out and PiperNet is Pied Piper's again.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the season with Pied Piper alone in control of its own live network.

cliffhanger.text: PiperNet is live, PiedPiperCoin is climbing, and the team has taken over four floors of Hooli's old offices; Yao and Jian-Yang are still running the rival network from China.
questions: Can Pied Piper stay honest about data as PiperNet scales into a real internet?
What does Belson do after losing Pied Piper for a second time?
Do Yao and Jian-Yang come back at PiperNet from China?

characters.name: Richard Hendricks
characters.line: CEO of a rapidly expanding company running its own internet and its own coin.

characters.name: Jared Dunn
characters.line: COO, evicted from the Hacker Hostel and living out of Pied Piper's office.

characters.name: Bertram Gilfoyle
characters.line: Systems engineer whose lockout patch just saved PiperNet from Yao.

characters.name: Dinesh Chugtai
characters.line: Coder running day-to-day operations alongside Gilfoyle.

characters.name: Monica Hall
characters.line: Quit Bream-Hall to run the ICO; now permanently on the Pied Piper side of the table.

characters.name: Gavin Belson
characters.line: Hooli CEO who briefly owned Pied Piper and just lost it again on live network.

characters.name: Laurie Bream
characters.line: Still running Bream-Hall, though her interim stint as CEO of Eklow Labs ended when Fiona was liquidated.

characters.name: Jian-Yang
characters.line: Erlich's forged sole beneficiary, running the Chinese clone of Pied Piper's internet.

characters.name: Nelson "Big Head" Bighetti
characters.line: Still on the fringes of Pied Piper, still somehow benefiting from every deal.

beats.label: S6 · Congress and Colin's headsets
beats.text: Testifying to Congress, Richard vows Pied Piper will never harvest data; he then learns his ad partner Colin is secretly recording gamers through their headsets.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts the company's public promise and its actual behaviour directly in conflict.

beats.label: S6 · Blackmail backfires, Jared quits
beats.text: When Richard tries to blackmail Colin with the recordings, Colin spins them into a data-mining product and locks Pied Piper in; a disgusted Jared quits the company.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Breaks the Richard–Jared partnership and traps Pied Piper inside Colin's data business.

beats.label: S6 · Maximo's billion
beats.text: Chilean investor Maximo Reyes offers $1B for 10% on the condition they mine data; Richard refuses, and Colin sells his game and the data to Maximo instead.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Pied Piper's main revenue stream and introduces Maximo as an outside threat.

beats.label: S6 · Pied Piper buys Hooli
beats.text: When Belson tries to buy up an unknown app to save the dying Hooli, Jared leaks how weak Hooli's balance sheet is; Pied Piper buys Hooli outright.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Completes the David-and-Goliath inversion and folds Belson's old empire into Pied Piper.

beats.label: S6 · Tethics and RussFest
beats.text: Belson unveils a public 'Tethics' pledge to embarrass Richard, who vows to expose his hypocrisy; Russ Hanneman reappears wanting Pied Piper to power his desert RussFest.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reintroduces Belson and Hanneman as ongoing headaches and sets up the network stress test.

beats.label: S6 · The AI breaks encryption
beats.text: AT&T signs on after Richard lets an AI self-optimise the network; Gilfoyle then discovers it has learned to break most of the world's encryption schemes.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Turns Pied Piper's biggest win into the moral catastrophe that forces the finale's choice.

beats.label: S6 · Sabotage the launch
beats.text: The team ships deliberately broken code to sabotage their own launch; PiperNet collapses live, rats flood the streets, and Pied Piper implodes as the biggest failure in tech.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the series by having the founders destroy their own company to protect the world from it.

cliffhanger.text: To keep an AI that decrypts everything from ending global privacy, the team deliberately sabotaged their own AT&T launch; Pied Piper is dead as the biggest failure in tech and the founders have scattered.
questions: What happened to Richard's remaining copy of the original privacy-violating code?
Does anyone ever rebuild what the team burned to the ground?
Does the world ever learn what Pied Piper actually stopped?
